Worlds. Every plugin includes `caddy-base`; the per-kind worlds add one
extension point each. A single binary may implement several kinds — write
your own world in your project that `include`s the ones you need, or use
`full-plugin`. The host does not require a specific world: it detects
which interfaces a binary exports and wires up only those.
Everything at once; mainly useful for reference and host testing.
Log a message with optional structured key/value fields.

Host-provided capabilities (imports, implemented by Caddy).
Structured logging into the plugin's zap logger.

The host creates a named logger per provisioned module, so log lines are
attributed just like native Caddy modules.

Replace all placeholders in the input, substituting `empty` for
placeholders that resolve to an empty value.
Resolve a single placeholder key.

The global Caddy replacer (placeholder resolution outside of a request
context). Request-scoped replacement is available on the `request`
resource in `http-types`.
Get a value by key. Returns none if absent or expired.

Set a key to a value. `ttl-ms` = time-to-live in milliseconds; none
means no expiration (lives until delete or config reload).
Delete a key. No-op if absent.

Atomic increment (creates with value `delta` if absent). Returns the
value after incrementing. `ttl-ms` applies only on creation (existing
TTL is preserved on increment). Useful for rate limiting.
Check existence without reading the value.

In-memory key-value store scoped to the plugin. Values are shared across
all pool slots (wasm instances) of the same provisioned module — unlike
guest-side linear memory, which is per-slot. NOT durable (lost on config
reload); for durable state use `host-storage`.

Typical use cases: rate-limiter counters (via `increment`), DNS record
caches, session data, circuit-breaker state, connection pools of
metadata.

No permission required (it's sandboxed per plugin — one plugin cannot
see another's keys).
Perform an HTTP request. `url` must be absolute http(s).

Host-provided network capabilities.

These interfaces are permission-gated: the host only honors them for
plugins whose manifest entry grants the corresponding permission
("http" / "tcp"). Without the grant, every call fails with a
"permission denied" error — the interfaces are always linkable so guests
can be compiled uniformly.
A simple synchronous outbound HTTP client (permission: "http").

This is deliberately much smaller than wasi:http — request and response
bodies are byte buffers, not streams. It is sized for API clients (ACME
DNS providers, object storage, webhooks), not for proxying large
payloads.
Dial `address` in Go net.Dial form, e.g. "redis.internal:6379".

Read up to `max` bytes. Blocks until at least one byte is
available, EOF, or the read deadline. Returns (data, eof).
Write bytes, returning the number written.

Set a deadline for subsequent reads/writes, in milliseconds from
now. 0 clears the deadline.

Raw TCP connections (permission: "tcp"), for protocols that are not
HTTP (redis, memcached, SMTP, ...). Synchronous, one connection per
resource handle.

Core guest interfaces every plugin must export: identity and lifecycle.
Plugin self-description. The host calls `describe` once at load time to
discover which Caddy modules this binary provides, and registers a
dynamic Caddy module for each declared ID.
Shared basic types used across interfaces.

Acquire a cluster-wide lock. Blocks until acquired or the host's
context is cancelled.

Access to Caddy's configured storage (mirrors `certmagic.Storage`).

This lets plugins persist state in whatever storage backend the Caddy
instance is configured with (filesystem, consul, redis, ...), including
cluster-safe locking.
Emit events onto Caddy's event bus (mirrors `caddyevents.App.Emit`).
Full request URI (path?query).
All header values, flattened.
Values for a single header name (canonicalized).
Rewrite the request URI (affects downstream handlers).

Read up to `max` bytes of the request body. Returns the bytes read
and whether the body has reached EOF.

Replace placeholders using the request-scoped replacer
(e.g. `{http.request.host}`).

Get/set request-scoped variables (caddyhttp vars middleware),
values serialized as JSON.
Set a response header. Must be called before write-status/write.
Write the status code. Implicitly 200 on first write otherwise.
Write body bytes. Returns bytes written.

Invoke the next handler in the middleware chain for this request.
This is what makes wasm handlers true middleware rather than
terminal-only handlers.

Invoke the next handler with a recording response writer instead of
the real one. Nothing is sent to the client; the guest receives the
buffered response and is responsible for writing output to the real
`response-writer` (headers from the buffered response are NOT copied
automatically). The buffered body is capped by the host (default
16 MiB); larger downstream responses fail the call.

HTTP request/response resources, owned by the host.

These are handles into the live `*http.Request` and
`http.ResponseWriter` — reads and writes go straight through to Caddy
with no copying of the full request across the boundary.

Provision a new instance of the module with the given ID from its
JSON config (= caddy.Provisioner).
= caddy.Validator.
= caddy.CleanerUpper. Called when the config is unloaded.

Module instance lifecycle, mirroring caddy.Provisioner / caddy.Validator /
caddy.CleanerUpper. The host creates one `instance` per provisioned
Caddy module and passes it back into every extension-point call.
= libdns.RecordGetter.
= libdns.RecordAppender.
= libdns.RecordSetter.
= libdns.RecordDeleter.

DNS provider (= libdns-style providers via `dns.providers.*` modules).

This unlocks the largest Caddy plugin category — ACME DNS-01 challenge
providers — as sandboxed wasm: a provider is pure API glue over the
registrar's HTTP API, so a guest needs only this export plus the
`host-http` import (permission: "http").

Semantics mirror libdns (https://github.com/libdns/libdns): all
operations are scoped to a zone (a fully-qualified domain name ending in
a dot), record names are relative to the zone, and each call returns the
records that were actually affected.
Event handler (= caddyevents handler modules, `events.handlers.*`).
Read up to `max` bytes. Returns bytes and whether EOF was reached.

Seek within the file. whence: 0 = start, 1 = current, 2 = end.
Optional: guests may return an error, which disables HTTP range
requests for files from this provider.

Filesystem provider (= io/fs.FS via caddy.fs modules, `caddy.fs.*`).

Lets wasm plugins back Caddy's file server (or any module that takes an
`fs` config) with arbitrary sources: object storage, databases, archives,
generated content, ...

Called by reverse_proxy on every request to get the current backends.
The request handle provides access to Host, path, headers, etc. so
the plugin can route by request attributes.

Dynamic upstream source (= reverseproxy.UpstreamSource, for modules in
`http.reverse_proxy.upstreams.*`).

This lets wasm plugins act as dynamic backends for Caddy's reverse_proxy:
given an incoming request, return the list of backend addresses to proxy
to. Combined with host-http and host-kv, a plugin can poll a service
registry and cache the results with TTL-based refresh.

Handle a request. Call `http-types.next` to continue the middleware
chain; don't call it to short-circuit.

HTTP extension points.
= caddyhttp.MiddlewareHandler, for modules in `http.handlers.*`.
= caddyhttp.RequestMatcherWithError, for modules in `http.matchers.*`.

Custom Caddyfile syntax (= caddyfile.Unmarshaler).

The host tokenizes the directive's segment of the Caddyfile and hands the
tokens to the guest, which returns the module's JSON config. This lets
wasm plugins define first-class Caddyfile directives without shipping a
full dispenser across the boundary.

Storage backend provider (= certmagic.Storage via caddy.StorageConverter,
for modules in `caddy.storage.*`).

The mirror image of `host-storage`: instead of consuming Caddy's storage,
the plugin *is* the storage backend (e.g. a wasm driver for an unusual
database or service).

A unique, storage-safe key identifying this issuer configuration
(= certmagic.Issuer.IssuerKey).
Issue a certificate for the given DER-encoded CSR.

TLS extension points.
Certificate issuer (= certmagic.Issuer, for modules in `tls.issuance.*`).

Combined with `host-storage`, this is enough to implement custom CAs,
internal PKI bridges, or exotic ACME-alikes entirely in wasm.

Certificate loader (= caddytls.CertificateLoader, for modules in
`tls.certificates.*`).
Total request timeout. Default: 30000.

Cap on response body size. Default: 16 MiB. Responses larger than
this fail the call.
Follow redirects (default: true, max 10 hops).

A standard-distribution directive name, e.g. "respond",
"file_server", "header".

Caddyfile directive ordering, mirroring Caddy's
httpcaddyfile.RegisterDirectiveOrder: a position relative to a
directive from the STANDARD distribution (Caddy deliberately forbids
ordering relative to other plugins, since plugin load order is not
guaranteed). Users can always override with the `order` global option.

Full Caddy module ID, e.g. `http.handlers.foo`. The namespace
prefix determines which extension-point interface the host will
invoke for instances of this module:

  http.handlers.*     -> http-handler
  http.matchers.*     -> http-matcher
  caddy.fs.*          -> fs
  tls.issuance.*      -> tls-issuer
  tls.certificates.*  -> tls-cert-loader
  caddy.storage.*     -> storage-provider
  events.handlers.*   -> event-handler
  dns.providers.*     -> dns-provider
  http.reverse_proxy.upstreams.* -> upstream-source
Optional human-readable description.

For `http.handlers.*` modules that also export the config
interface: where this module's Caddyfile directive should be
ordered. Absent = host default (before file_server).
Plugin name, for diagnostics.
JSON-encoded text. Caddy module configs are JSON documents.
Milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

An error returned from a plugin, with an optional HTTP status hint.

When returned from an HTTP handler this maps to
`caddyhttp.Error(status, err)` on the host side.
True if the key is a leaf (a value, not a directory-like prefix).
A key stored in a storage backend (mirrors `certmagic.KeyInfo`).
Unique event ID (UUID).
The module ID of the event's origin.
Event data serialized as JSON.
An event on Caddy's event bus (mirrors `caddyevents.Event`).

A fully-buffered downstream response, produced by `next-buffered`.
This is what enables response-rewriting middleware (replace-response,
caching, compression): inspect status/headers/body, then write a
(possibly modified) response through the real `response-writer`.
RR type, e.g. "TXT", "A", "CNAME".
Name relative to the zone (e.g. "_acme-challenge.www").
Priority for types that use it (MX, SRV, ...).
Abort the event (= caddyevents.ErrAborted).
Any other failure.
Unix-style mode bits.
An open file, owned by the guest.
Network address to dial, e.g. "192.168.1.10:8080" or "unix//tmp/app.sock".
Optional maximum concurrent requests to this upstream. 0 = unlimited.

True if the token was quoted (or heredoc'd) in the Caddyfile.
Needed to distinguish a literal "{" argument from a block brace
(mirrors caddyfile.Token.Quoted()).
PEM-encoded certificate (chain).
Optional metadata stored alongside the certificate.
Arbitrary tags used to select certificates.

caddy:plugin — a generic plugin interface for the Caddy web server.

This package mirrors Caddy's own extension model: a plugin declares one or
more Caddy modules (identified by namespaced IDs like `http.handlers.foo`,
`caddy.fs.bar`, `tls.issuance.baz`), each configured with a JSON document,
provisioned/validated/cleaned-up by the host, and invoked through a
namespace-specific interface.

A single wasm binary may export any subset of the extension-point
interfaces below; the host inspects the binary's exports and only wires up
what is present.
